analysis.summary: The PR introduces several high-severity runtime crash risks and incorrect error handling by assuming API responses always contain nested data structures and hardcoding success responses.

bugs.title: Runtime crash on failed order retrieval in Salesforce path
bugs.description: The code performs unsafe nested property access on 'response-data' immediately after calling getUserOrder. If the API call returns an error structure (e.g., 404 or 500) that lacks the 'response-data' key, the application will crash with a TypeError.
bugs.risk: In the event of any downstream service failure or missing order, the Lambda will crash with a 500 Internal Server Error instead of returning the proper error information to the client.

bugs.title: Hardcoded success response and runtime crash risk in CPI orders
bugs.description: The handler now hardcodes 'code: 200' and 'info: SUCCESS' while extracting 'response.Responses.SPTResponse'. If postCPIOrder returns an error or a structure without 'Responses', the code will crash. If it returns an error structure that happens to have the 'Responses' key, the API will incorrectly report success to the caller.
bugs.risk: Critical failure in error propagation; failed order creations will either crash the service or be reported as successful to Salesforce/callers, leading to data inconsistency.

notBugs.reason: While stripping standard headers (like Authorization) in the Salesforce path is risky, it appears to be an intentional design choice for this specific endpoint to map query parameters to headers for compatibility.
All variables (queryParamsData, headersData, pathParamsData, response) are properly declared at the handler scope and assigned within both branches of the conditional logic.
